response:
Both measurement campaigns are complete and the suite has run. Here is my report.

---

# Panel review: two proposed extraction fixes

**Method.** Full suite run (4,674 passed, 4 skipped, **2 failed — both fail identically with the patch stashed**: one asserts the canonical repo has a `.git` directory, which a disposable worktree copy doesn't; one detects ledger drift against uncommitted sim logs. Neither is caused by these changes). Re-parsed all 2,492 archived replies under `bench/logs/**/round_*.json` with both parser versions loaded side by side, then read every reply whose output changed.

## Fix 1 — field-label verdicts (`_VERDICT_RE`): **VERIFIED**

**Reproduced.** 6,132 → 6,867 verdicts (+735) over 2,492 replies including sims; the author's +734/2,414 is the same result minus one `DeepSeek-SIM` reply. Per-model breakdown matches **exactly**: Gemini 368, Codex 177, ChatGPT 154, DeepSeek 29, CC2 6. **Zero of the 6,132 pre-existing matches are lost or altered** (keyword position and captured groups identical — I asserted this per match, not per count).

**Is it too permissive?** In principle yes — I constructed false positives the alternative admits: `SEE ALSO: CONFIRM C0125`, `WHY WE CANNOT: CONFIRM C0125 — reason`, `I REFUSE TO: CONFIRM C0125` all now match. In practice, **zero occur**: the labels on all 735 recovered lines are `VERDICT` (445), `FIND` (135), `DESCRIPTION` (134), `FINDING_ID` (19), `PROPOSED_FIX` (2), and I sampled every label class — all are unambiguous verdict assertions, including the odd-looking `FINDING_ID: CONFIRM C0001` (a Gemini habit) and both `PROPOSED_FIX` cases. Negation without a colon (`DO NOT CONFIRM C0125`) correctly does not match. The risk is theoretical; the recovery is real.

**Verdict-without-evidence is the right outcome.** A CONFIRM attaches to a canonical entry that already carries the description, fix, and falsifier; registering the block as a *finding* would re-mint a duplicate of that canonical — the exact defect the P3 (Exp 38) skip exists to prevent. I also verified the safety interlocks: CONFIRM/CHALLENGE/MERGE tallies all reduce to *distinct models* (`confirm_models`, merge quorum), so a verdict caught twice in one reply cannot inflate any status transition; `MERGE C#### <- F###` same-line sources are still captured (separator class includes `<`/`-`); and a verdict-only reply in this shape can't fall through to an UNSTRUCTURED junk finding because the C-id it cites trips the registry-prose guard.

**Three anomalies not named in the brief:**
1. **The two verdict recognizers have now drifted apart.** `runner_core`'s fallback-suppression regex (`_has_verdicts`, arm 5) was *not* taught the field-label shape. Today the C-id prose guard happens to cover it; that is coincidence, not design. Sync them or import one from the other.
2. **Fence-blindness.** 19 of the 735 recovered verdicts (and 115 of the 6,132 pre-existing) sit inside ``` fences. All I inspected are genuine (Gemini fencing its whole structured reply), and this pre-dates the fix — but the verdict parser has no fence awareness at all, and a model quoting instructions could cast verdicts.
3. `**DESCRIPTION:** CONFIRM C0125` (bold-wrapped label) is *still* missed — `_parse_verdicts` never runs `_normalise_field_labels`. Not a regression; noting for completeness.

## Fix 2 — markdown-heading arm 4b: **REFUTED as implemented** (problem real, gating right, implementation should be replaced)

**The diagnosis and the gate placement are correct, and I confirm:** the exp43 C0040 reply parses identically under the new code (no exp43 reply changes at all); verdict-titled headings are skipped; and the re-used-F-id hazard is neutralized by existing machinery — `lookup_alias` turns a re-listed id into a self-CONFIRM, which `independent_count` excludes. In exp39's round-3 "Combined Review Synthesis", F001–F003 pre-exist from rounds 0–2, so only F004 (a genuine finding) would newly register in a live run.

**But two of its supporting claims are false, and its harvest detracts from the schema:**

1. **"Exactly 1 of 2,401 real replies uses this shape" is wrong by 7×.** Running the actual parser, **7 real-archive replies change**: exp30 r01/r07, exp31 r08, exp37 r00/r15, exp39 r03, exp42 r00. (The rehearsal numbers also don't reproduce: I measure round 0 of `sim45…003907Z` at 3→12 findings, 2→6 agents, not 4→17.) The direction *favors* the fix — exp30 r07 is literally headed "## NEW FINDINGS (Applying FFF Protocol)" and every recovery I read is genuine content that previously vanished or was blobbed into a sev-0.3 UNSTRUCTURED sentinel — but a fix justified by measurement must measure with the instrument it changes.

2. **It strands the recovered findings without their schema fields.** Those same replies carry `FLAW_CLASS` (2,3,4,5,7), chevron `FIX` blocks up to ~2.2 kB, and resolvable target files. Arm 4b hardcodes `flaw_class=1`, drops `proposed_fix` and `target_file` entirely — starving the Bugzilla close-loop, the fix-efficacy probe, and corrected-copy supply, i.e. precisely the *tools-decide* machinery — and in 2 of the 7 real cases (exp37 r00, exp42 r00) writes `SEVERITY:/FLAW_CLASS:` metadata into `description`, reintroducing the "metadata read as claim" defect class explicitly repaired on 2026-08-17.

**On the specific questions.** Severity default 0.5 is safe against *manufacturing* criticals (threshold 0.7) but inverts the deliberate 0.7 choice of the existing 1B.3 DeepSeek header adapter and can *suppress* a critical stated only in words — "(Critical)" in a title maps to nothing (word-severity normalisation covers only full-line `SEVERITY: word`). Empirically every affected archived body carried a numeric severity, so no archived harm. `flaw_class=1` is defensible only because the arm can't read the body's stated class; the alternative below reads it.

**The change I would make instead — demonstrated, not proposed:** follow the codebase's own 1B.3 precedent. Behind the identical `if not findings:` gate, rewrite `^#{1,6}\s*F\d+ — title` headings into synthetic `FINDING_ID:`/`DESCRIPTION:` lines and re-run the marker arm once. I implemented this and swept the full archive: it fires on **exactly the same 23 replies** (7 real + 16 sim), zero others, and on every one it dominates arm 4b — correct flaw_class, `target_file` = `bench/runner_core.py` / `bench/dm/_types.py` / `bench/cdsfl_registry/composer.py`, fixes up to 2,171 chars recovered, and clean FIND-derived descriptions in both corrupted cases — while inheriting the P3 verdict-skip, code-leak guards, chevron extraction, and falsifier-attachment keys for free. Two blemishes to iron out before adoption: a chevron block whose `<<<<` line carries code can yield a code-line as `target_file` (pre-existing marker-arm behavior; fails safe downstream), and when both a title and a `FIND` field exist the description can trail into the metadata lines (fixable by emitting the synthetic `DESCRIPTION` after the block's field lines, or adding `SEVERITY`/`FLAW_CLASS` to the description terminator set).

**Bottom line.** Fix 1 enhances the schema; adopt it. Fix 2 is a real bug correctly diagnosed and correctly gated, but as written it recovers findings in a form the framework's own verification machinery cannot act on — in a project whose deliverable is tool-verified findings, that is a detraction relative to an alternative the codebase already contains a precedent for. Replace arm 4b with the gated heading→marker adapter and re-measure.
